question: Does a 'Center Ridge' (Easy 5th) exist on Mount Jefferson, and if not, which route is it under a wrong name?
answer: It exists as a named entry, but as an old name for another route: Mountain Project route 106064240 'Center Ridge' (Easy 5th, Mod. Snow, Grade III, FA unknown) is on the west face, starting from the PCT on the west side and following the ridge directly to the summit pinnacle, shaded all morning. A 2012 comment says it is usually called the West Rib in the Oregon High guidebook; a 2015 comment says an older Nick Dodge guidebook calls it Center Ridge. Our logged ascent 844314 was a West Rib from the Woodpecker Ridge side, consistent. It is not the South Ridge nor the Southwest Ridge. Our stored row has no text, so nothing contradicts this.
recommendation: Keep the row, rename it West Rib (alt name Center Ridge), alpine, Easy 5th, face West, season snow-dependent, fill text in our words. Do not merge with South Ridge; the duplicate suspicion in the track notes is not supported.

proposed.name: West Rib
proposed.overview: A direct ridge on the west face leading to the summit pinnacle, climbed with moderate snow below and good rock on the pinnacle. It needs no protection until the pinnacle, stays shaded all morning, and is usually done with pickets or screws on the snow ridge plus nuts and slings above.
proposed.approach: Reach the ridge from the west side off the Pacific Crest Trail, from either Pamelia Lake or the Woodpecker Ridge side. Expect a long approach; check which trailhead and permit applies before going.
proposed.descent_text: Descend the same ridge, or traverse north around the pinnacle to the east side where loose fourth-class rock leads down. Watch for rockfall.
